Folks — I ran a quick independent harness on behalf of Edge.AI and saw the same TTFT delta Alex reported when switching from a Triton-based baseline to the Redwood runtime image. Two quick notes that often explain this pattern:

- Triton sidecar/service-level batching can hide setup latency (it coalesces multiple requests at the transport layer) which skews TTFT lower.
- Your tokenization pipeline adds a few special tokens for control metadata; if the Redwood harness uses a different tokenizer config the effective sequence length increases ~5–12 tokens which compounds TTFT and throughput.

I’ve uploaded our run csv (ttft-concurrency-results-20260615.csv) to the shared Drive. Happy to join the sync.

Best,
Daniel Lopez
Benchmarking Engineer, ThirdPartyBench

Subject: Re: RE: Request: MAP + benchmark plan and initial numbers

Alex / team — I dug into the harness differences and attached step-by-step repro instructions (repro-steps-triton-vs-serve.md). Summary of what I ran for parity:

- Test harness: we used the same request traces you provided; tokenization aligned to the "edge-vocab-v2" you shared. Confirmed no extra control tokens.
- Warmup: measured TTFT as both cold-first-byte and steady-state (10-request warmup). Cold-first-byte is consistently higher; our MAP will capture both metrics separately.
- Flags: disabled Triton-level batching and forced single-request scheduling to replicate per-request latency.
- Quantization: we used 4-bit quant profile Q4_2 for parity; changing profile shifts throughput by ~8–15% in our tests.

Observed discrepancies and remediation:
- Your runs were performed with Triton batching enabled; when I disabled it, TTFT increased and aligned with our numbers. Action: Edge to re-run with "--triton-batching=false" or use our harness.
- Memory cliff at 12 streams looks like a kernel-scheduling artifact on your GPU driver version (470.x). Neha will validate memory behavior on 510.x which we use in Dedicated.

Next steps I recommend we scope into the MAP doc (redwood-map-v1.pdf):
- Reproduce parity run (owner: Edge infra / Redwood bench) — due 6/15
- Joint tuning pass (owner: Karthik / Edge infra) — due 6/18
- Final handoff and capacity commit (owner: Marissa / Alex) — due 6/25

Let me know when you can run the disabled-batching job; I’ll standby to analyze the output.

-Karthik
Principal Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
